It has been reported that isolated CPUs can suffer from interference due to
per-CPU kworkers waking up just to die.
A surge of workqueue activity during initial setup of a latency-sensitive
application (refresh_vm_stats() being one of the culprits) can cause extra
per-CPU kworkers to be spawned. Then
running merrily on an isolated CPU only to be interrupted sometime later by
a kworker marked for death (cf. IDLE_WORKER_TIMEOUT
kworker activity).
Prevent this by affining kworkers to the wq_unbound_cpumask (which doesn't
contain isolated CPUs
column2: cf. HK_TYPE_WQ) before waking them up after marking

Changing the affinity does require a sleepable context
introduced pool->idle_cull_work to get that.

separate list. This intentionally prevents for_each_loop_worker() from
iterating over workers that are marked for death.
